title: Deferred-emit and transient checkpointing for hosted streaming silences
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Several enterprise customers have reported streaming responses from the Hosted API that terminate with partial outputs or silence for 5–30s before the final token is emitted, or never emit the final segment at all. In some cases SDKs surface truncated transcripts; in others the client receives a final empty event and gives up. This ticket captures the technical investigation, root cause, proposed mitigation (deferred-emit + transient checkpointing), rollout plan, and follow-ups for customer communication and SDK patches.

Observed customer symptoms:
- Mid-stream silence for requests with long-running generation (>8s) followed by either (a) delayed final token (10–45s later) or (b) no final token and connection close.
- Some customers see duplicate tokens after reconnects; others observe missing trailing punctuation or cut sentences.
- Correlated with higher proxy idle-close counts and a subset of large-batch kernel executions on NVMe-backed nodes.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
- Two contributing issues observed in logs and flamegraphs: (1) an intermittent race between the runtime's final-flush path and the gateway's chunk-assembly: when kernel emits final KV blocks near the gateway timeout boundary, the gateway may mark the connection as idle and tear down before the buffered final-chunk flush completes; (2) the current streaming path emits chunks immediately as produced, with minimal end-of-stream atomics, so transient network/proxy closes can cause the last chunk to be lost without an idempotent marker.
- Secondary exacerbator: micro-batching and asynchronous append-to-sse queue means final tokens can be enqueued but not drained if a proxy sends a FIN.

Proposed technical mitigation (deferred-emit + transient checkpointing):
1) Deferred-emit window: hold the last N (configurable, default 2) chunk(s) in a short-lived, in-memory staging buffer at the gateway for up to T seconds (configurable, default 10s) after emission. If the SSE connection closes unexpectedly, attempt to replay the staged chunks on a reconnect or surface a deterministic final marker to the client SDK to trigger a fetch/completion call.
2) Transient checkpointing: write lightweight, idempotent final-token markers to the request-level metadata store (fast in-memory tier with replication to local node) when generator reaches EOS. The marker contains a compact checksum and sequence number that clients/SDKs can use to detect missing tail tokens and request backfill via a short completion API.
3) Idempotent final marker in stream: emit a small, distinct final event (finality-v1) after the last token is flushed from the runtime. The marker is signed by the gateway and includes sequence and checksum. Clients will treat this as authoritative end-of-stream.
4) Backfill path: implement a server-side completion endpoint (GET /v1/streams/:id/complete) that, given a stream id and final marker, returns any staged or persisted trailing tokens. This is intended as an emergency reconciliation used by SDKs when they detect a missing final marker.

Compatibility and SDK impact:
- Minimal: SDKs should add a reconnect/backfill flow: on connection close without finality-v1, call the completion endpoint with the stream id and accept deduplicated trailing tokens. We'll ship a patch to official JS/Python SDKs in parallel.

Canary & rollout plan:
- Feature-flag gated at gateway layer: deferred-emit off by default.
- Step 1 (canary): enable for a single internal tenant + two small enterprise tenants for 48h, collect metrics (finality-emit-rate, backfill-calls, staged-chunk-memory).
- Step 2: widen to 10% of hosted API traffic for 72h, observe latency p50/p95 for streaming requests and memory pressure on gateway nodes.
- Step 3: enable by default for all hosted API traffic with runtime release runtime-1.21 if metrics are stable.

Telemetry & metrics to add before canary:
- finality_marker_emitted (count, by model, by region)
- staged_chunk_count_per_request (histogram)
- backfill_requests_total (count, result: hit/miss)
- gateway_idle_closes_by_proxy
- per-request end-to-end time between runtime EOS and finality_marker (latency gauge)

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for the staging buffer and marker emission logic; property tests for idempotency and replays.
- Integration test that simulates FIN during final flush and asserts backfill returns missing tokens.
- Chaos test: inject random proxy idle closes and verify no customer-visible truncation for long-lived streams.
- Load test: verify staging window memory under 10% feature rollout at 95th percentile workloads.

Rollout safety & mitigations:
- If gateway memory increases beyond threshold, reduce staging window T or number of staged chunks N via runtime config.
- If backfill hit rate rises unexpectedly, throttle backfill calls with a lightweight rate limiter per tenant to avoid thundering retries.
- Provide an escape hatch: kill-switch to turn off deferred-emit and final-marker emission globally.

Follow-ups and customer communications:
- Patch SDKs (JS/Python) with backfill flow and test helpers (diego/pr/1234).
- Inform customers with active escalations (CS case IDs: CS-9812, CS-9907) and offer temporary Dedicated routing while feature is in canary for high-risk tenants.
- Confluence doc: /confluence/hosted-streaming/deferred-emit-design (drafted)
- Postmortem-style incident notes consolidated into internal incident tracker: incident-2025-02-stream-sillence (owner: Priya Singh).

Acceptance criteria (before marking Done):
- Canaries show <0.1% incidence of missing final markers for affected tenants and no regressions in p95 latency.
- SDK patches published and validated by at least two customers.
- Feature flag and kill-switch documented and ops runbook updated.
- Dashboard tiles show finality_marker_emitted, backfill_requests_total, and staged_chunk_memory.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Diego Morales: Investigated gateway logs for CS-9812. Found multiple FINs with pending enqueued writes inside the SSE drain queue. Reproduced locally with tcpkill + local proxy. Created WIP sketch for staging buffer and marker format.
2025-02-24 - Priya Singh: Customer impact confirmed high for two enterprise tenants. Recommend P0 and immediate canary prioritization. Added labels and requested SDK support ticket.

2025-02-26 - Diego Morales: Prototype implemented: in-memory staging buffer + finality marker emitted. Integration test added that simulates FIN during flush — test passes locally. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4581 (draft).

2025-02-28 - Security review (note): final marker contains no plaintext customer data, only checksums and seq ids. Security okayed staging buffer retention (temporary) but asked to add an opt-out for regulated customers. (Reviewer: Mona Patel)

2025-03-02 - QA: Ran chaos test with proxy-fin injection across 50 parallel streams. Backfill path returned missing tokens 98% of failures. Observed 1.8% increase in gateway memory under 10% rollout simulation. Plan to tune default T from 10s -> 6s for canary.
2025-03-04 - Diego Morales: Updated prototype to expose staging window T via feature flag. Prepared canary checklist and created monitor dashboards. Creating customer comms draft for CS team.
